record.title: The missing-digits product-set interval conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a missing digits set, meaning a compact set determined by restricting the digits in a fixed integer base. **Folklore conjecture.** If

$$
\dim_{\mathrm{H}} K>1/2,
$$

then $K\cdot K$ contains intervals. This is presented as a folklore conjecture, and Theorem 3 can be viewed as a partial answer; its general status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Han Yu, “Missing digits points near manifolds”, arXiv:2309.00130 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00130

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

record.title: Individual fractional covering conjecture for looms
record.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be hypergraphs forming an $(r,s)$-loom, and write $\mathbb{L}=(A,B)$. Let $\tau^*(A)$ and $\tau^*(B)$ denote their fractional covering numbers.

**Loom component conjecture.** Then

$$
\tau^*(A)=s,\qquad \tau^*(B)=r.
$$

The source states that this would imply the preceding loom conjecture in the equal-uniformity case and would force $|V(A)|=|V(B)|=rs$. It remains open.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Eli Berger, Joseph Briggs, He Guo and Shira Zerbib, “Looms”, arXiv:2309.03735 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.03735

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2023). “The conjecture is open for $r\ge 4$.”

record.title: Aouchiche–Hansen Randić index diameter bound
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, with Randić index $\operatorname{R}(G)$, diameter $\operatorname{d}(G)$, and order $\#V(G)$. **Aouchiche–Hansen's conjectured bound.**

$$
\operatorname{R}(G)\geq \operatorname{d}(G)+\sqrt{2}-\frac{\#V(G)+1}{2}.
$$

This is a proposed lower bound relating the Randić index to graph diameter. The supplied source does not state whether the bound has been resolved.
record.source_name: Margaret I. Doig, “Block eccentricity, a radius bound, and an application to the Randić index”, arXiv:2309.11613 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.11613

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

record.title: Havet's chromatic conjecture for trees with few leaves
record.statement: Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $\ell\in\mathbb N$, let $D$ be a digraph, and let $T$ be an oriented tree with $k$ edges and $\ell$ leaves. **Havet's conjecture.** Every $(k+\ell)$-chromatic digraph contains every oriented $k$-edge tree having $\ell$ leaves. This generalizes Burr's chromatic conjecture and the tournament conjecture for trees with few leaves; it is known only in restricted cases.
record.source_name: Maya Stein, “Oriented trees and paths in digraphs”, arXiv:2310.18719 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.18719

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

record.title: Ruskey's Hamiltonian-path conjecture for the graph of linear extensions
record.statement: Let $P$ be a finite sign-balanced poset, and let $\mathcal G(P)$ be the graph whose vertices are the linear extensions of $P$ and whose edges correspond to adjacent switches. **Ruskey’s conjecture.** The graph $\mathcal G(P)$ has a Hamiltonian path. This conjecture concerns Gray-code generation of linear extensions; the source cites algorithmic work and surveys but does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Swee Hong Chan and Igor Pak, “Linear extensions of finite posets”, arXiv:2311.02743 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.02743

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

record.title: Abrishami, Henning, and Rahbarnia's bipartite cubic planar domination conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite cubic planar graph, and let $\gamma(G)$ denote its domination number. **Abrishami, Henning, and Rahbarnia's conjecture.**

$$
\gamma(G) \leq \frac{|V(G)|}{3}.
$$

This is described in the paper as a weaker version of Zhu and Wu's conjecture; the source gives no resolution of it.
record.source_name: Eun-Kyung Cho, Eric Culver, Stephen G. Hartke and Vesna Iršič, “Domination of subcubic planar graphs with large girth”, arXiv:2312.03384 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03384

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2023). “It is now known that the conjecture is false in general, but Henning and Dorbec showed that it holds for graphs with girth at least $9$.”

record.title: The power conjecture for componentwise polymatroidal ideals
record.statement: Let $I\subset S$ be a componentwise polymatroidal ideal in a polynomial ring $S=K[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. **Power conjecture.** Every power $I^k$ of $I$ has linear quotients. The source gives this as an expectation after noting that products of componentwise polymatroidal ideals need not remain componentwise polymatroidal; no resolution is supplied in the provided text.
record.source_name: Antonino Ficarra, “Shellability of Componentwise Discrete Polymatroids”, arXiv:2312.13006 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.13006

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2023). “The converse is an open question :”

record.title: Conjecture on fractional list packing for planar triangle-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar triangle-free graph. The **fractional list-packing conjecture.**

$$
\chi_\ell^\bullet(G) \le 4.
$$

This conjecture would extend the paper's list-coloring results to fractional packing numbers and would imply an improved flexibility bound for planar triangle-free graphs. It is presented as an open problem.
record.source_name: Stijn Cambie, Wouter Cames van Batenburg and Xuding Zhu, “Disjoint list-colorings for planar graphs”, arXiv:2312.17233 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.17233

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2023).

record.title: Eventual three-term representations by generalized pentagonal numbers
record.statement:
Let $p_m(x)$ and $\bar p_m(x)$ denote the generalized polygonal-number functions used in the paper, and let $\mathbb N$ denote the nonnegative integers. **Eventual representation conjecture.** The following four inclusions hold:

$$
\{p_5(x)+p_5(y)+p_5(z):x,y,z\in\mathbb N\}\supseteq\{n\in\mathbb N:n>33066\},
$$

$$
\{\bar p_5(x)+\bar p_5(y)+\bar p_5(z):x,y,z\in\mathbb N\}\supseteq\{n\in\mathbb N:n>24036\},
$$

$$
\{p_6(x)+p_6(y)+p_6(z):x,y,z\in\mathbb N\}\supseteq\{n\in\mathbb N:n>146858\},
$$

$$
\{\bar p_6(x)+\bar p_6(y)+\bar p_6(z):x,y,z\in\mathbb N\}\supseteq\{n\in\mathbb N:n>138158\}.
$$

These conjectures assert explicit eventual universality for four ternary sums of generalized polygonal numbers. The notation $p_m$ and $\bar p_m$ is not defined in the supplied context, and no proof or resolution is given.
record.source_name: Zhi-Wei Sun, “New results similar to Lagrange's four-square theorem”, arXiv:2411.14308 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.14308

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).

record.title: The induced rainbow path conjecture for triangle-free graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple triangle-free graph, let $\chi(G)$ be its chromatic number, and let $\phi:V(G)\to[k]$ be a proper vertex coloring, where $k=\chi(G)$. A path in $G$ is **rainbow** if all its vertices have distinct colors under $\phi$, and **induced** if no two nonconsecutive vertices of the path are adjacent in $G$. **Induced rainbow path conjecture.** Every colored triangle-free graph $(G,\phi)$ contains an induced rainbow path on $\chi(G)$ vertices. This would simultaneously strengthen the known existence of induced paths and rainbow paths of order equal to the chromatic number in colored triangle-free graphs. The conjecture remains open in general, although several partial results are known.
record.source_name: N. R. Aravind, Shiwali Gupta and Rogers Mathew, “Towards a conjecture on long induced rainbow paths in triangle-free graphs”, arXiv:2601.00602 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.00602

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2026). “While this conjecture remains open in general, several partial results are known.”

record.title: The strengthened polynomial log-concavity conjecture for independent-set polynomials
record.statement:
Let $M=(E,\mathcal{I})$ be a matroid with rank $r_M$, and let $f_k(M)$ be its degree-$k$ independent-set polynomial

$$
f_k(M)=\sum_{I\in\mathcal{I},\,|I|=k}\left(\prod_{x_i\in I}x_i\right).
$$

For $0<k<r_M$, **the strengthened polynomial log-concavity conjecture.**

$$
f_k^2(M)\geq\left(1+\frac{1}{k}\right)f_{k-1}(M)f_{k+1}(M).
$$

This is motivated by Dowling's polynomial conjecture and the second inequality in Mason's conjecture, and is attributed in the source to an implicit conjecture of Zhao. The supplied text does not state a resolution, so its status remains open.
record.source_name: Shiqi Cao, Keyi Chen, Yitian Li and Yuxin Wu, “Dowling's polynomial conjecture for independent sets of matroids”, arXiv:2601.03809 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03809

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2026). “The third inequality in Conjecture , known as Mason's ultra log-concavity conjecture, was independently proved by Anari, Liu, Oveis Gharan and Vinzant , and by Br{\"a}nd{\'e}n and Huh .”

record.title: Ball's weak cylinder conjecture for point sets in finite affine 3-space
record.statement: Let $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^3$ be a set of $p^2$ points, where $p$ is prime. The **cylinder** condition means that $S$ is the union of $p$ pairwise disjoint parallel lines, and hence has size $p^2$. The **weak cylinder conjecture.** If the number of non-determined directions of $S$ satisfies $|N_S|\geq p$, then $S$ is a cylinder. This is one of Ball's proposed forms of the cylinder conjecture over prime fields. The problem concerns the structure of sets with few determined directions in higher-dimensional finite affine spaces and is presented in the source as an open question.
record.source_name: Gergely Kiss, Ádám Markó, Zoltán Lóránt Nagy and Gábor Somlai, “Cylinder type and p-divisible sets in F_p^3”, arXiv:2601.09910 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.09910

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).

record.title: Ball's strong cylinder conjecture for p-divisible sets in finite affine 3-space
record.statement: Let $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^3$ be a set of $p^2$ points, where $p$ is prime. The set $S$ is **$p$-divisible** if every affine hyperplane in $\mathbb{F}_p^3$ intersects $S$ in a number of points congruent to $0\pmod p$. A **cylinder** is the union of $p$ pairwise disjoint parallel lines. The **strong cylinder conjecture.** If $S$ is $p$-divisible, then $S$ is a cylinder. The strong form replaces the directional hypothesis of the weak form by the algebraic condition of $p$-divisibility; the source presents it as an open problem.
record.source_name: Gergely Kiss, Ádám Markó, Zoltán Lóránt Nagy and Gábor Somlai, “Cylinder type and p-divisible sets in F_p^3”, arXiv:2601.09910 (2026).
record.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).

record.title: Strengthened list-size conjecture for proper conflict-free coloring
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph distinct from $C_5$, and let $L$ be a list assignment of $G$. For each vertex $v$, assume that

$$
|L(v)|=\begin{cases} 4\quad &\text{if}\quad d_G(v)=2\quad \text{and}\\ d_G(v)+1\quad &\text{if}\quad d_G(v)\neq 2. \end{cases}
$$

Here a coloring is **proper conflict-free** when it is both proper and conflict-free. **Strengthened list-size conjecture.** Then $G$ is proper conflict-free $L$-colorable. This is proposed as a common strengthening of the preceding degree-plus-one and degree-plus-two conjectures; the source presents it as open.
record.source_name: Masaki Kashima, Riste Škrekovski and Rongxing Xu, “Degree-choosability of proper conflict-free list coloring of sparse graphs”, arXiv:2601.15611 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.15611

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).

record.title: The non-Borel–Cantelli sequence conjecture for drawable graphs
record.statement:
Let $\textbf{p}\in(0,1)^\omega$ be a sequence that is not Borel–Cantelli. The notation $\Sigma_{\mathbf{p}}$ denotes the class of objects drawable using the sequence $\mathbf{p}$.

**Non-Borel–Cantelli sequence conjecture.** If $\textbf{p}\in(0,1)^\omega$ is not Borel–Cantelli, then

$$
\Sigma_{\mathbf{p}}=\varnothing.
$$

The conjecture concerns the characterization of drawable graphs and is motivated by the preceding proposition and related work on random graphs. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Ziemowit Kostana, Jarosław Swaczyna and Agnieszka Widz, “Infinite random graphs”, arXiv:2601.16013 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.16013

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).

record.title: Center-representing minimal graph conjecture for Lie algebras
record.statement: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional minimal-graph-admissible Lie algebra with non-trivial center $\mathcal{Z}(\mathfrak{g})$. **Center-representing graph conjecture.** The Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ admits a minimal graph $G(V,E)$ such that the set of all vertices with no outgoing edges spans the center $\mathcal{Z}(\mathfrak{g})$. A preceding construction represents the center using an extended graph, but it is generally not minimal; the conjecture asks whether minimality can be retained.
record.source_name: Tim Heib and David Edward Bruschi, “On the structural properties of Lie algebras via associated labeled directed graphs”, arXiv:2601.16161 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.16161

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2026). “We now present a selection of open problems and conjectures that naturally arise from our findings.”

record.title: Finest-granularity magma-graph faithfulness conjecture
record.statement: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex finite-dimensional Lie algebra and $(\mathcal{M},\delta)$ an abelian magma such that $\mathfrak{g}$ is $\mathcal{M}$-magma-graded with finest granularity. Let $G_{\mathfrak{g}}(V,E)$ be the graph obtained from this pair by the modified graph-construction algorithm. **Finest-granularity faithfulness conjecture.** The graph $G_{\mathfrak{g}}(V,E)$ faithfully represents the internal structure of $\mathfrak{g}$ in the seven senses listed in the source: solvability, derived series, nilpotency, lower central series, ideals, simplicity, and semisimplicity. The source explicitly places this statement among open problems and conjectures, so it remains open.
record.source_name: Tim Heib and David Edward Bruschi, “On the structural properties of Lie algebras via associated labeled directed graphs”, arXiv:2601.16161 (2026).
record.references:

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2026). “We now present a selection of open problems and conjectures that naturally arise from our findings.”

record.title: Apte–Parekh–Sud token-excess matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph, let $F_k(G)$ be its $k$-th token graph, and define

$$
\operatorname{\varepsilon}_k^T(G)=\lambda_1(L(F_k(G)))-|E|.
$$

Let $\nu(G)$ denote the matching number of $G$. **Apte–Parekh–Sud's token-excess conjecture.** For $1\le k\le |V|$,

$$
\operatorname{\varepsilon}_k^T(G)\le \nu(G).
$$

This conjecture is stated after the paper's bounds for token graphs; those bounds do not establish the proposed matching-number upper bound, and the supplied status gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Alan Lew, “An approximate version of Brouwer's Laplacian conjecture”, arXiv:2601.17575 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17575

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2026). “In particular, they showed that the sum of the $k$ largest eigenvalues of the Laplacian matrix of a graph $G$ is bounded from below by the sum of the $k$ largest degrees of $G$.”

record.title: Short rainbow circuit conjecture for regular matroids
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a simple regular matroid, let $r(M)$ denote its rank, and let $c$ be an $(r(M)+1)$-colouring of $M$. A rainbow circuit is a circuit whose elements have pairwise distinct colours. It is **short** when

$$
|C|\leq \left\lfloor \frac{r(M)+2}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

**Short rainbow circuit conjecture.** If $(M,c)$ has no colour-singular elements, then $M$ has a short rainbow circuit.
This conjecture extends the corresponding rank-two case from graphs to regular matroids. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Sean McGuinness, “Short Rainbow Circuits in Regular Matroids”, arXiv:2601.17624 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17624

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).

record.title: Perfect-power conjecture for the plane partition function
record.statement: Let $pl(n)$ denote the plane partition function, counting plane partitions of $n$. A **perfect power** is an integer of the form $a^b$ with integers $a,b>1$. **The plane-partition perfect-power conjecture.** The plane partition function $pl(n)$ is never a perfect power of the form $a^b$ for integers $a,b>1$. This is proposed as an analogue of Sun's conjecture for plane partitions and remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Summer Haag, Praneel Samanta, Swati, Holly Swisher, Stephanie Treneer and Robin Visser, “Repellent properties of perfect powers on partition functions: a heuristic approach”, arXiv:2601.18138 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18138

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2026). “This conjecture has been verified for all $n \leq 10^8$ by Alekseyev , but still remains an open problem.”
